analysis.file_name: USA_ Core Retail Sales Above Expectations.pdf
analysis.title: USA: Core Retail Sales Above Expectations; Boosting Q4 GDP Tracking to +2.4%; PCE-Relevant Component of Import Prices Slightly Softer
key_insights: Core retail sales (ex-autos, gasoline and building materials) rose 0.6% m/m in October, above the +0.3% median forecast and GS's +0.2%. The September level was revised up 0.7%, reflecting a +0.37pp revision to September growth and +0.36pp to August.

Core retail strength was led by miscellaneous store retailers (+4.7%), health and personal care stores (+1.5%) and nonstore retailers (+1.2%). Headline retail sales rose 0.2% vs the +0.1% median, helped by gasoline (+1.5%, third straight strong month) and held back by motor vehicles and parts (-1.6%).

GS estimates the three-month annualized pace of real core retail sales growth rose to +8.4% from +6.5% in September. It attributes the resilience to tax refunds and equity-market wealth effects, which more than offset the drag from higher energy prices.

GS expects steady consumer spending growth in 2027 (+2.2% Q4/Q4). Support comes from gradually easing inflation pressure and a modestly positive fiscal impulse from tax refunds and the reversal of benefit cuts.
Industrial production fell 0.4% in October vs the +0.1% median and GS +0.2%, driven by a -4.3% drop in utilities. Utilities output is the source data for consumption in GDP.
Manufacturing production rose 0.3%, above the +0.2% median. Gains were concentrated in autos (+4.4%), furniture (+1.8%) and computer and electronic products (+1.4%).

High-technology industries (semiconductors, computers, communications equipment) rose 2.1% in October and 14.3% over the last year. Capex-sensitive business equipment rose 1.0% in October and 7.8% over the year.

Capacity utilization edged down to 76.4% from 76.8%. GS says most manufacturing industries operate well below peak capacity, and only electrical equipment and machinery are nearing peak rates, likely reflecting AI-related demand.

GS raised its Q4 GDP tracking estimate by 0.6pp to +2.4% (quarter-over-quarter annualized) and its past-quarter (Q3) tracking estimate by 0.3pp to +3.8%. Retail sales and industrial production details were stronger than prior assumptions on net.

Core import prices rose 0.8% in October vs the +0.5% median, and headline import prices rose 1.1% vs +0.7%. The surprise came from semiconductor (+6.9% m/m, SA by GS) and computer peripherals and parts (+4.0%) prices.
GS reads the import price data as further AI-related price pressure, and estimates its impact on year-over-year core inflation will peak at the end of 2026.

International airfares in import prices rose 0.4% (SA by GS). GS now estimates October core PCE prices rose 0.29% m/m (from 0.30% before the release), or +3.24% y/y, and headline PCE rose 0.32% m/m, or +3.83% y/y. The PCE figures are GS estimates, not official prints.
